newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ford, Koc move to equalise stakes in Otosan.
newsitem.headline: Ford, Koc move to equalise stakes in Otosan.

text.p: Two companies within Turkey's leading industrial conglomerate Koc Holding said they would sell their small stakes in Turkish car and commercial vehicle producer Otosan to Ford Motor Company.

The move is part of Ford and Koc Holding's agreement late last year to equalise their stakes in their joint venture Otosan. Koc group's total stake is 53.86 percent while Ford's is 30 percent in Otosan's 1,392.5 billion lira capital.
Koc's durables producing arm and Turkey's biggest Arcelik and automotive casting unit Doktas are to sell their Otosan stakes to Ford, according to their statements.

Arcelik said it would sell 7,684,908 shares, or 1.38 percent of Otosan's capital for $5.26 million. Doktas said it would sell 14,035,078 shares, or 2.52 percent of Otosan's capital, for $9.60 million.
Sales procedures are expected to be completed by July 24 after approval by the Treasury's Foreign Investment directorate.

Arcelik said a 746.25 billion lira profit expected from the sale at current lira/dollar rates would be used to raise capital while Doktas awaits a 1.37 trillion lira sale profit, also planned to be used in a capital increase.
After the sale, Doktas will still hold a 0.27 percent stake in Otosan.
